items.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997
items.q: And this drummer named Jimmy Cappers kept saying, “why don’t you play free — why don’t you play free things?”

ctx.x: Very, quite free. and I was wondering if this is how you went into this record, and said we’re really going to — I don’t know what phrase to use — push the envelope here.

No, I think I was pretty much doing that kind of thing because I had Michael Moore with me, who was very much into, like he wrote several of those tunes. It’s funny, after a while Michael Moore became very conservative and I always felt bad because it seemed like he led me into this and every time somebody’s around that it’s going to be a little free – I’ll fall back in. I mean I can’t really do it by myself. I’m trying to think exactly when it happened. I think I was playing a place called The Apartment, it was…

made “Ambiance” anyway, and before I had Michael Moore. And this drummer named Jimmy Cappers kept saying, “why don’t you play free — why don’t you play free things?” And I really couldn’t sort of quite understand what it was I had to do, and I kept trying and I’d always end up in a triad or something. And finally I was able to do that very thing. I mean I can do it. But at that time I probably never would have thought of doing “Piano Jazz” with Cecil Taylor. But it’s funny now I love doing that. But I don’t know…
